preflight.unavailable: Preflight checks are unavailable right now.
preflight.blocked: Upgrade blocked: fix the failing checks first.
preflight.upgradeCommand: Run this on the server (never runs automatically)
preflight.rollbackCommand: To roll back the database after a bad upgrade
preflight.waiting: This release is still being published. Nothing is wrong with your server: re-check in a few minutes.

history.olderWhy: These releases support an older database format than yours, so they are not offered as upgrades. Going back to one means restoring a backup, which loses data written since.
history.title: Release history and rollback
history.description: The last five releases. Pick one to preview exactly what returning to it would do. Nothing is applied from this page: a rollback is run on the server so the control plane never replaces itself.
history.empty: No releases found for this channel.
history.emptyHint: Switch to another channel above, or check that this host can reach github.com.
history.githubUnreachable: GitHub could not be reached. Showing cached releases and the binaries kept on this host.
history.currentSchemaUnknown: Database schema version could not be read

plan.title: Rollback to {{version}}
plan.description: A read-only preview. Nothing has changed.
plan.loading: Checking this release against your database...
plan.loadError: Could not build the rollback plan: {{message}}
plan.targetUnknown: {{version}} does not publish a schema version.
plan.downtime: Estimated downtime: about {{seconds}} seconds while the service restarts.
plan.blocked: Blocked: fix the failing checks below before rolling back.
plan.changesTitle: What you give up between {{target}} and {{current}}
plan.noChanges: No release notes are available for the releases in between.

verdict.binary_only: Safe: the database schema matches, so only the program is replaced. Your data is untouched.
verdict.forward: This release is newer than your database and will migrate it forward when it starts. That is an upgrade, not a rollback.
verdict.restore_required: A binary-only rollback is not possible. This release is older than your database schema and would refuse to start. The only way back is to restore a database backup, which permanently loses everything written after it.
verdict.unknown: This release does not publish its database schema version, so compatibility cannot be confirmed. An older program refuses to start on a newer schema without touching data, and the previous release is restored automatically if that happens.

step.backup: Take a fresh backup of the control plane database
step.fetch: Download the release and verify its checksum and signature
step.verify: Re-check the retained binary against its recorded checksum
step.stop: Stop the control plane (apps keep running)
step.restore_backup: Replace the database with the backup you choose
step.verify_health: Wait for health and readiness checks to pass
step.auto_recover: If it does not become healthy, put the previous release back automatically

warning.data_loss: Data written after the chosen backup is lost for good.
warning.forward_migration: The database will be migrated forward.
warning.no_compatible_backup: No local backup is old enough for this release, so a rollback to it is not possible from here.
warning.dev_build: This is a development build, so the running binary cannot be kept for rollback.

dataLoss.title: This loses data
dataLoss.body: Restoring replaces the database with a backup. Anything written after the backup is lost, including deploys, settings changes and audit entries. The database you have now is kept beside it as a copy, and a fresh backup is taken first.
dataLoss.noneCompatible: No backup on this host is compatible with {{version}}.

commands.fetch: 1. Stage the verified release on the server
commands.apply: 2. Roll back on the server (you will be asked to type {{version}})
commands.restore: Roll back and restore the backup on the server

plan.backupHint: Backups older than a day are flagged above. A fresh backup is also taken automatically before anything changes.

oneClick.unavailable: This rollback cannot be applied from the dashboard: {{reason}}
oneClick.confirmBody: The control plane takes a backup, swaps the program and restarts. Apps keep running. If the old release does not become healthy, the current one is restored automatically.
oneClick.started: Rollback to {{version}} started. The dashboard reconnects when the control plane is back.

verify.title: Verify after an upgrade or rollback
verify.description: Runs the control plane's own health checks and reports a clear result. Run it once the service is back.

upgradeHistory.title: Upgrade history
upgradeHistory.description: Every version this control plane has run, recorded when it started, however it was installed. Nothing upgrades silently: acknowledge each change once you have seen it.
upgradeHistory.empty: No upgrades recorded yet: the first one will appear here.
upgradeHistory.emptyHint: A new row is added whenever the control plane starts on a different version.
upgradeHistory.pendingBody: These version changes have not been acknowledged by anyone yet. Check what changed, then acknowledge each one.
upgradeHistory.unacknowledged: Not acknowledged yet. Someone should confirm this change was expected.
upgradeHistory.initiatorUnknown: Initiator unknown: nothing recorded who changed the version (no installer note was left).
upgradeHistory.schemaMoved: The database schema changed. Returning to the previous version needs a database restore, which loses data written since.
upgradeHistory.notesUnavailable: Release notes were not available at the time

restorePoints.title: Restore points
restorePoints.description: A restore point (database copy, program and service file) is taken automatically before every upgrade. Restoring puts back the program, and the database only if the running one was already changed by a newer release.
restorePoints.empty: No restore points yet. One is taken automatically before the next upgrade.
restorePoints.confirmWithData: The program and the database go back to how they were at {{time}}. Everything saved since then is discarded. The replaced database is kept on the host.
restorePoints.confirmBinaryOnly: The program goes back to the earlier release. The database is already compatible, so no saved changes are lost.
restorePoints.started: Restoring {{version}} on the host. The result appears in the upgrade attempts above.

selfUpgrade.dbRestored: The database was restored from the snapshot. {{minutes}} minutes of changes made since the snapshot were rolled back.
selfUpgrade.dbKept: The database was already compatible with the previous release, so no changes were lost.
selfUpgrade.title: Upgrade this server
selfUpgrade.description: Downloads the release, checks its checksum and signature, backs up the database, tries the migrations on a copy, swaps the program and restarts. If the new release does not become healthy in time, the previous program and data come back automatically.
selfUpgrade.noPlan: No upgrade plan is available right now. The latest release could not be fetched.
selfUpgrade.notesMissing: The release notes could not be fetched, so breaking changes cannot be checked from here. Run the host command shown below once you have read them.
selfUpgrade.noBreaking: No breaking changes are declared between these versions.
selfUpgrade.ackFirst: Acknowledge every breaking change to enable the upgrade.
selfUpgrade.safety: A snapshot of the database and the current program are kept first. A bad release is rolled back without you doing anything. Data written to the control plane during the health window of a failed upgrade is not kept.
selfUpgrade.started: The upgrade is running on the host. This page reconnects when the control plane restarts.
selfUpgrade.hostOnly: This host cannot run the upgrade from the dashboard: {{reason}}.
selfUpgrade.hostCommand: Run on the server as root
selfUpgrade.noAttempts: No upgrades have run on this server yet.
selfUpgrade.rolledBackNote: The previous release {{version}} is running again and its data was restored.
selfUpgrade.notPinned: Release signatures are verified by this server. The next upgrade checks the signature, then this install only accepts signed releases.
selfUpgrade.pinned: Signed releases only, pinned since {{version}}. An unsigned release is refused.
selfUpgrade.noAttemptsHint: When you upgrade from this page or on a schedule, each attempt shows up here with every step it took.

failure.title: What went wrong

cause.disk_full: The server ran out of disk space.
cause.network: The release could not be downloaded.
cause.checksum_mismatch: The downloaded file did not match its checksum.
cause.signature_invalid: The release signature could not be verified, so it was refused.
cause.binary_unusable: The new program did not pass its start-up probe.
cause.backup_failed: The pre-upgrade backup could not be taken.
cause.migration_incompatible: The database migration dry run failed.
cause.service_control: The service could not be stopped or started.
cause.swap_failed: The new program could not be put in place.
cause.not_healthy: The new release did not become healthy.
cause.guard_refused: The upgrade was refused before it started.
cause.unknown: The step failed for a reason this page does not recognise.

failure.fixed: Cleanup finished. You can retry now.
failure.stillFailing: Cleanup ran but the problem is still there.
failure.started: Started on the host. Follow it in the timeline.
failure.cliHint: Run on a machine logged in to this server:

readiness.title: Server readiness
readiness.description: Who holds ports 80 and 443, Docker version and isolation, exposed Docker API, disk, memory, firewall and DNS, with the install mode this server needs.
readiness.failed: The readiness check could not run: {{message}}

mode.own_ports: Recommended: install with its own ports 80 and 443
mode.behind_proxy: Recommended: install behind your existing proxy

channel.description: Which release stream to compare against and, if enabled, check in the background. Checking never applies an update by itself.
channel.autoCheckHelp: This only controls whether the control plane periodically checks and shows a notice when a newer release is available. A release is applied only when you start or schedule an upgrade, or when automatic upgrades below are turned on.

upgradeNow.fixFirst: Fix the blocked checks above to enable the upgrade.
upgradeNow.blockedTitle_one: 1 check needs attention before you can upgrade
upgradeNow.blockedTitle_other: {{count}} checks need attention before you can upgrade
upgradeNow.waitingTitle: Waiting for the release to finish publishing
upgradeNow.schemaBlockedTitle: Not offering {{version}}: it is older than your database

hero.aheadTitle: You are running a development build
hero.aheadBody: You are running a development build (schema {{schema}}). The latest release, {{latest}}, is older than your data, so there is nothing to upgrade to. The next release that includes your data format will be offered automatically.
hero.aheadBodyNoSchema: You are running a development build. The latest release, {{latest}}, is older than your data, so there is nothing to upgrade to. The next release that includes your data format will be offered automatically.
hero.rollbackNoneWhy: No restore point for an older version exists on this host yet.
hero.planMigrationsUnknown: Database migrations: not reported by the release
hero.planRestorePoint: A restore point is taken first, so the previous version and its data can come back.
hero.planVerify: The new release has {{seconds}} seconds to prove it is healthy before it is kept.

upgradeNow.confirmDescription: This server will go from {{current}} to {{target}}. Your apps keep running.
upgradeNow.willBackup: A backup of the control plane database is taken and kept before anything changes.
upgradeNow.willRestart: The control plane restarts once. This page reconnects by itself.
upgradeNow.willRollback: If the new release is not healthy in time, the previous program and its data come back automatically.
upgradeNow.reconnect: The control plane restarts during the upgrade. This page keeps checking and reloads once the new release answers.

progress.waiting: Starting the upgrade on the host...
progress.reconnecting: The control plane is restarting. Reconnecting, this can take up to two minutes.
progress.rolledBack: The previous release {{version}} is running again and its data was restored.
progress.untouched: Nothing was changed: {{version}} is still running.
progress.nextAction: Fix the cause above, then upgrade again from this page, or run the command shown on the host.

schedule.dialogDescription: The checks run again at the scheduled time. If any fails, nothing is applied, you are alerted, and it retries until the grace period ends.
schedule.noWindow: No maintenance window is configured. Set one under Automatic upgrades, or pick a time.
schedule.majorAck: I understand this is a major version jump and may not be reversible without a restore.
schedule.firesNote: Only a root session or token can schedule or cancel. Every change is written to the audit log.

auto.title: Automatic upgrades
auto.description: Off by default. When on, the control plane schedules new releases into your maintenance window and applies them with the same checks, backup and rollback as a manual upgrade.
auto.unavailable: The automatic upgrade policy is available to root sessions and tokens.
auto.modeHelp: Releases with breaking changes that need your acknowledgement, and major version jumps, are never applied automatically.

mode.off: Off (upgrade only when I start or schedule it)
mode.any: Any new release on the configured channel

notice.off: Automatic upgrades are off. This control plane upgrades only when you start or schedule an upgrade.
notice.patch: Automatic upgrades are on for patch releases. New patch releases are applied inside your maintenance window after the minimum release age.
notice.any: Automatic upgrades are on for any new release on the channel. Releases are applied inside your maintenance window after the minimum release age.
notice.paused: Automatic upgrades are paused. Nothing is applied automatically until you resume.

auto.minAgeHelp: Wait this many days after a release is published, so early regressions are caught by others first.
auto.notifyNone: No notification channels yet. Alerts still go to every enabled channel once you add one.
auto.notifyHelp: Where scheduled, held and failed upgrade notices go. With none selected, every enabled channel is used.
auto.edgeUnavailable: Automatic upgrades are not available on the edge channel: edge builds are container images, not signed release binaries. Switch the channel to beta or stable to use them.

stable.label: Stable (recommended)
stable.description: Signed releases that are ready for everyday use.

beta.label: Beta (pre-release)
beta.description: Signed pre-releases with new features, a little earlier than stable.

edge.label: Edge (latest main, unstable)
edge.description: A container image of the newest commit on main. Not signed, can break, container installs only.

version.latestEdge: A newer edge build is available: {{version}}
version.upToDateEdge: You're on the latest edge build.
version.edgeHostBinary: Edge is a container image channel. This control plane runs as a host binary, so it cannot follow edge.

edge.title: Edge is a container image
edge.intro: Edge builds are container images, not signed binaries, so there is no release or checksum to verify.
edge.compose: Or pin it in your compose file
edge.binaryTitle: Edge cannot be installed on this host
edge.binaryBody: Edge builds cannot be installed on a host binary. Switch to a channel that ships signed binaries.

page.title: Updates
page.description: Current version, release channel, and available releases.
page.errorBody: The updates page could not load: {{message}}. Your server keeps running. Try again in a moment.
page.sourceNote: Compared against the published releases on GitHub.

status.checkFailedBody: The release source could not be reached: {{message}}. Your server is unaffected. Check that this host can reach github.com, then try again.
status.inProgressBody: The upgrade is running. This page reloads when the new release answers.

changes.title: What changes if you upgrade
changes.notesEmpty: Release notes are not available yet.

settings.channelDescription: Which release stream this server follows.
settings.backgroundDescription: Look for new releases on a schedule and show a notice.
settings.backgroundLabel: Check for updates in the background

pipeline.rolledBack: Rolled back to {{version}}, your data is intact.

result.succeeded: Upgraded from {{from}} to {{to}} at {{time}}, verification passed
result.succeededUnverified: Upgraded from {{from}} to {{to}} at {{time}}, verification did not complete
